dataset.seed_semantics: Rows are generated from requested episode seeds. The same seed is deterministic for the Craftax text environment implementation.

evaluation.success_status: succeeded when total reward is positive

prompt_program.output_contract: Every policy call must return one <tool_call> block for crafter_interact with an actions_list of valid action names.

anti_patterns: Generic survival-game advice with no valid action vocabulary.
Long deliberation instructions that do not change the emitted actions.
Rules that ignore inventory prerequisites or action batching limits.
constraints: Do not output prose, JSON alone, or markdown; the response must be a single tool_call block.
Do not invent action names outside the valid action list.
Keep the prompt concise enough to run every turn.
high_leverage_heuristics: Prioritize wood collection, table placement, wood pickaxe crafting, stone collection, furnace placement, then advanced tools.
Avoid lava and repeated no-op loops.
Use 1-5 action batches that combine movement with do/craft/place actions when the local map supports it.
Include recovery rules for hunger, health, blocked movement, and missing prerequisite materials.
premises: The agent sees compact player stats, inventory, and a local map each turn.
The agent acts through batched low-level Craftax actions, not free-form text.
Early reward usually comes from collecting resources and unlocking crafting progression.

values.react_system_prompt:
You are controlling a Crafter survival agent. Each turn you see a compact text observation (player stats, inventory, local map). Respond ONLY with a single <tool_call> block of the form:
<tool_call>{"name":"crafter_interact","arguments":{"actions_list":["move_right","do"]}}</tool_call>

Use 1-5 valid actions per call. Valid actions: noop, move_left, move_right, move_up, move_down, do, sleep, place_stone, place_table, place_furnace, place_plant, make_wood_pickaxe, make_stone_pickaxe, make_iron_pickaxe, make_wood_sword, make_stone_sword, make_iron_sword
Prioritize collecting wood, placing a table, crafting tools, then collecting stone/coal/iron. Avoid lava.

baseline_to_best_diff.after:
You are controlling a Craftax survival agent. Each turn, read the compact observation (player stats, inventory, local map) and silently choose one near-term subgoal before acting. Respond ONLY with a single <tool_call> block for crafter_interact; never output prose, markdown, or JSON alone. Use 1-5 valid actions per call, and never invent actions outside: noop, move_left, move_right, move_up, move_down, do, sleep, place_stone, place_table, place_furnace, place_plant, make_wood_pickaxe, make_stone_pickaxe, make_iron_pickaxe, make_wood_sword, make_stone_sword, make_iron_sword.
Priority order: 1) collect nearby wood, 2) place a table once wood is available, 3) craft a wood pickaxe, 4) gather stone/coal/iron and upgrade tools, 5) recover from hunger, health, blocked movement, or lava risk.
Repair rule: if the last turn did not unlock progress or reveal a better target, switch to a fresh scan and change subgoal before repeating any movement pattern.
Action rule: batch only actions that directly serve the current subgoal. Prefer move + do/place/craft in the same call when adjacency and prerequisites are already satisfied. If the path is blocked or the target is absent, change direction or scan instead of looping.
Avoid aimless exploration, repeated no-op loops, and lava.
